faq.q: Why do babies have more bones than adults?
faq.a: Babies are born with around 300 bones and bony pieces, many partly made of cartilage. As they grow, many of these fuse together, so an adult ends up with 206.
asks: How many bones does a baby have?

faq.q: What is the soft spot on a baby's head?
faq.a: The soft spots, called fontanelles, are gaps between the skull plates covered by tough membrane. They let the skull flex during birth and grow with the brain, and they usually close by about 18 months to 2 years.
asks: Why is a baby's skull soft?

faq.q: Which bones fuse together as we grow?
faq.a: Skull plates join together, three bones fuse into each hip bone, five vertebrae fuse into the sacrum, a few tiny ones form the tailbone, and the ends of long bones fuse to their shafts.
Fusing happens at different times for different bones. Most growth plates close in the late teens, and a few, like the collarbone, finish fusing in the mid-twenties.
asks: At what age do bones stop fusing?
When is the skeleton fully grown?

faq.q: How many bones does an adult have?
faq.a: An adult usually has 206 bones, though the exact number can vary slightly from person to person, for example with an extra small bone in the foot or an extra rib.
asks: Does everyone have the same number of bones?

facts: A newborn has roughly 270 to 300 bones and bony parts; an adult usually has 206 bones.
The sacrum forms from five vertebrae that fuse together.
